automation_builder.description: Manychat-style visual flow builder for trigger/action automations. Creators build automations to handle commerce, community, content, email, and schedule events without code. This is a full visual programming environment scoped to creator workflows.
automation_builder.implementation_note: No automation-related pages, components, schema tables, or API routes exist anywhere in the codebase. The PRD names it as Module 11. Workflow 7 ('Set up automations') is listed as NOT IMPLEMENTED.

visual_flow_editor.description: Drag-and-drop canvas where creators assemble automation flows from triggers, conditions, and actions. Each flow is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of nodes connected by edges.

ui_model.design_reference: X/Twitter minimalism — clean node cards with minimal chrome, monochrome with accent color for active/selected states
ui_model.sidebar: right-panel node property editor, appears on node click
ui_model.toolbar: top bar with save, test, activate/deactivate toggle, name/description

ai_features.description: CreatorOS AI is UTILITY-LEVEL, not agent-level. AI assists the human creator with content creation, scheduling, recommendations, and moderation. The creator is always in control. AI never acts autonomously on business decisions.
ai_features.boundary_principle: AI as tool, not agent. Every AI feature has a human approval step before any external-facing action. AI suggests, creator approves.

content_suggestions.description: AI-powered content idea generation based on creator's niche, audience demographics, trending topics, and past performance data. Generates post drafts, titles, captions, and hashtag sets.
content_suggestions.model_requirements: General-purpose LLM (GPT-4o-mini or equivalent). Low token usage per request. No fine-tuning required.
content_suggestions.user_flow: Creator opens content studio -> clicks 'Get AI suggestions' -> AI generates 3-5 ideas -> creator picks one -> AI drafts post -> creator edits and publishes
content_suggestions.cost_model: Per-request to LLM API. Estimated $0.001-0.01 per suggestion batch. Included in Pro tier; limited on Free tier.
content_suggestions.current_code_note: OpenAI SDK (openai 4.91.1) is a dependency. Basic chat completion exists in AI agent feature. No content suggestion UI or API endpoint.

smart_scheduling.description: AI analyzes historical engagement data to recommend optimal posting times per platform. Accounts for audience timezone distribution, day-of-week patterns, and content type performance.
smart_scheduling.model_requirements: Can be deterministic (statistical analysis) with AI enhancement for explanation. Does not require LLM for core scheduling — regression/heuristic model is sufficient.
smart_scheduling.deterministic_fallback: Default to platform best-practice times (e.g., Instagram: 10am-2pm local, Twitter: 8am-10am local) when insufficient historical data. This is the spine.
smart_scheduling.user_flow: Creator schedules post -> AI recommends 'Best time: Tuesday 10:30am (your audience is 73% US Eastern)' -> creator accepts or overrides
smart_scheduling.current_code_note: No scheduling UI, no calendar component, no engagement analytics aggregation.

audience_insights.description: AI-generated audience analysis: demographic breakdowns, engagement patterns, growth trends, content preference signals. Summarized in natural language with charts.
audience_insights.model_requirements: Statistical analysis layer (deterministic) + LLM for natural language summary. Heavy lifting is SQL aggregation, not AI.
audience_insights.deterministic_fallback: Raw metric dashboards with numbers and charts. AI adds the narrative layer ('Your audience grew 12% this week, driven by your tutorial posts').
audience_insights.current_code_note: No analytics dashboard beyond basic revenue numbers. No follower demographic tracking in schema.

auto_moderation.description: AI-assisted content moderation for community channels and comments. Detects spam, hate speech, self-promotion, and policy violations. Flags for human review (never auto-removes without creator policy).

tiers.method: Keyword blocklist + regex patterns + rate limiting
tiers.action: Auto-flag or auto-hide based on creator's policy
tiers.note: This is the spine — always active, zero AI cost

tiers.method: LLM classification of flagged content for context-aware judgment
tiers.action: Reclassify false positives, detect subtle policy violations
tiers.note: Only invoked for content that passes deterministic layer but has low confidence

creator_controls.custom_rules: Creator-defined keyword lists and regex patterns
creator_controls.appeal_flow: Moderated users can appeal; creator reviews and overrides

auto_moderation.current_code_note: No moderation UI, no moderation table in schema. Module 16 (Moderation) listed as NOT IMPLEMENTED.

ai_search.description: Unified search across all creator content, products, communities, and profiles with AI-enhanced ranking and typo tolerance.

search_domains.note: Scoped to user's accessible conversations only

approach.deterministic_layer: PostgreSQL full-text search (tsvector/tsquery) for keyword matching. This is the spine.
approach.ai_enhancement: Optional semantic search via embeddings for 'related content' and 'you might also like' features. Not required for MVP.
approach.ranking: Recency + relevance + creator authority score (follower count, engagement rate)

ai_search.current_code_note: No search UI, no search API endpoint, no full-text indexes in schema.

ai_vs_eos_boundary.description: Clear delineation between EOS agent architecture and CreatorOS AI utility features. These are fundamentally different paradigms.

eos_agent_system.description: EOS has a full autonomous agent framework: CEO agent, specialized sub-agents, task delegation, authority engine, governance, spine execution pipeline, multi-model intelligence routing, and recursive self-improvement. Agents can reason, plan, and execute multi-step workflows autonomously within governance bounds.
capabilities: Intelligence routing across providers (cc_sdk -> Gemini -> Groq -> Ollama)
Memory and learning (trace recording, feedback loops, quality scoring)
eos_agent_system.integration_model: UMH substrate — agents ARE the system

creatoros_ai_system.description: CreatorOS uses AI as a utility/assistant layer. AI generates suggestions, the human creator decides. No autonomous execution. No agent identity. No delegation. AI is a tool in the creator's toolkit, like a calculator or spell checker — powerful but always human-driven.
capabilities: Post draft writing (creator edits before publishing)
Audience insight summaries (SQL aggregation + LLM narrative)
Content moderation assistance (deterministic spine + AI enhancement)
Search ranking (full-text search + optional semantic layer)
AI agent product type (creator builds chatbots for their audience)
creatoros_ai_system.integration_model: API calls to LLM providers. No substrate integration. No agent framework. AI is stateless per-request unless chat history is explicitly stored.

key_differences.eos: Agents act autonomously within governance bounds
key_differences.creatoros: AI only acts when creator explicitly requests; never autonomous

key_differences.eos: Named agents with soul documents, roles, and authority domains
key_differences.creatoros: Anonymous utility functions — no agent identity

key_differences.eos: Agents make and execute decisions (with risk classification)
key_differences.creatoros: AI suggests, creator decides. Always human-in-the-loop.

key_differences.eos: Persistent memory, learning loops, trace recording
key_differences.creatoros: Stateless per-request (except AI agent chat history stored in ai_chats.messages JSON)

key_differences.eos: CEO agent delegates to specialist sub-agents
key_differences.creatoros: No agent hierarchy. Single LLM call per feature.

key_differences.eos: Full governance: risk classes, authority engine, accountability
key_differences.creatoros: No governance layer. Creator is the only authority.
Direct OpenAI SDK call. Single provider. No fallback chain.

key_differences.eos: Per-agent-call via subscription (cc_sdk) or API keys
key_differences.creatoros: Per-feature-request. Costs passed through or absorbed in tier pricing.

overlap_area.description: The AI agent product type is the one area where both systems touch AI chatbot functionality. EOS has multi-provider, governance-wrapped agents. CreatorOS has simple OpenAI-powered chatbots creators sell to consumers. These must NOT be conflated.
overlap_area.eos_agents: Internal business operations agents — they work FOR the entrepreneur
overlap_area.creatoros_agents: Sellable AI chatbot products — creators BUILD them, consumers USE them. No governance, no authority, no autonomous action.

open_questions.description: Decisions that require operator input before implementation can proceed.

questions.question: Should automation builder be available on all pricing tiers or gated to Pro ($29) and above?
questions.context: Manychat gates advanced automations behind paid plans. ConvertKit includes basic automations in free tier. Whop includes automation in all plans.
options: Free: 1 active automation, 100 executions/month. Pro: unlimited automations, 10K executions/month. Business: unlimited everything.
Pro and above only. No automation on Free tier.
All tiers get automation. Differentiate by trigger types (Free gets basic triggers only).
questions.recommendation: Option 1 — limited free tier with usage caps drives conversion to Pro while letting creators experience the value.

questions.question: What job queue / background processing system for automation delays and scheduled sends?
questions.context: Automation wait_delay and cron_schedule triggers need reliable background job processing. Current stack has no job queue.
options: BullMQ (Redis-backed, Node.js native, well-supported with Drizzle)
pg-boss (PostgreSQL-backed, no Redis dependency, simpler ops)
Inngest (managed serverless, event-driven, good DX but external dependency)
questions.recommendation: pg-boss — keeps everything in Neon Postgres, zero new infrastructure, sufficient for creator-scale automation volumes.

questions.question: Should CreatorOS AI features use OpenAI exclusively or support multiple providers via model_router pattern?
questions.context: Current code imports openai SDK directly. EOS uses model_router with multi-provider fallback. CreatorOS is a separate TypeScript application, not a UMH substrate consumer.
options: OpenAI only (GPT-4o-mini for cost efficiency). Simplest implementation.
OpenAI primary + Anthropic fallback. Two providers for resilience.
Abstract AI provider interface in TypeScript, similar to model_router pattern. Future-proof but more engineering.
questions.recommendation: Option 1 for MVP — OpenAI only via existing SDK. Abstract later if cost or availability becomes an issue. CreatorOS AI is utility-level; provider diversity is not critical.

questions.question: How should AI feature costs be allocated across pricing tiers?
questions.context: AI content suggestions, smart scheduling explanations, and audience insights use LLM tokens. At GPT-4o-mini pricing (~$0.15/1M input, $0.60/1M output), costs are low per request but can accumulate with high usage.
options: Free: 10 AI requests/month. Pro: 500/month. Business: 5000/month. Enterprise: unlimited.
Free: no AI features. Pro: included (soft cap at 1000 requests). Business/Enterprise: unlimited.
All tiers get AI. Hard cap per tier with option to buy more credits.
questions.recommendation: Option 1 — gives free tier a taste of AI features, Pro tier generous enough for daily use, Business handles power users.

questions.question: What sender domain strategy for CreatorOS email?
questions.context: SendGrid requires verified sender domains. Options range from shared domain (mail.creatoros.com) to creator custom domains. Domain reputation directly affects deliverability.
options: Shared domain (mail.creatoros.com) for all tiers. Simplest setup, shared reputation risk.
Shared domain for Free/Pro, custom domain support for Business/Enterprise.
Custom domain required for all creators (higher setup friction, best deliverability).
questions.recommendation: Option 2 — shared domain gets creators started fast, custom domain for serious creators who need deliverability control.

questions.question: Email subscriber limits per pricing tier?
questions.context: ConvertKit: Free up to 10K subscribers. Mailchimp: Free up to 500. Beehiiv: Free up to 2.5K.
options: Free: 500 subscribers. Pro: 5,000. Business: 25,000. Enterprise: unlimited.
Free: 1,000 subscribers. Pro: 10,000. Business: 50,000. Enterprise: unlimited.
No subscriber limits. Charge per email sent instead.
questions.recommendation: Option 2 — generous free tier (1K) to compete with Beehiiv/ConvertKit for creator acquisition. Revenue comes from Pro tier.

questions.question: Should search include semantic/AI-powered search in MVP or stay with PostgreSQL full-text search only?
questions.context: PostgreSQL tsvector/tsquery provides solid keyword search with stemming and ranking. Semantic search (embeddings) adds 'find similar content' but requires embedding storage and vector search (pgvector or external service).
options: PostgreSQL full-text search only. Fast to implement, zero additional cost, covers 90% of use cases.
PostgreSQL full-text search + pgvector for semantic similarity. Neon supports pgvector extension.
External search service (Meilisearch, Typesense, Algolia). Best search UX but operational overhead.
questions.recommendation: Option 1 for MVP — PostgreSQL full-text search covers keyword search needs. Add pgvector semantic layer later when 'related content' and 'you might also like' features are prioritized.
